pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
test 'AC-2' checks / and ?view=open list only open items in id order.
test 'AC-3' checks done-only, ✓-marked, in id order (marks 3 then 1, expects 1,3).
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order with ✓ only on done.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__.

Behaviour is implemented and tested, but no test names AC-7: the last commit (e9a514b 'Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-7: an empty table…' to drop the id, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. By the naming rule the item is unmet.
traffic/routes.json lists both; test 'AC-8' imports routes.json and asserts them.

findings.what: The 'Follow-up edits' commit removed the 'AC-7:' prefix from the test that proves the empty-table and empty-view messages, so no test names AC-7. The PR body still claims the test file covers AC-1 to AC-8.
findings.fix: Restore 'AC-7' in the test title (e.g. 'AC-7: an empty table says so in every view; …').

findings.what: PR claim 'test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8' is not true of the named tests after the last commit (AC-7 unnamed).
findings.fix: Fix the test title; the claim then holds.

lenses.note: Spec exists with go dated 2026-10-12; decisions (open default, query parameter) followed, no cookie.
All state-table rows have tests; AC-7 loses its test name in the last commit.
Tests assert behaviour and would fail on wrong code. I did not run them; CI covers that. The traffic fake-app change and the config-check tests cover the new query-string routes.
README updated for the views; no stale references found.
Object.hasOwn guards __proto__; the query is built from a fixed table, not from user input; the empty-table check is correct.
Titles are escaped; view is whitelisted; no injection path. The regex change allows '?' in routes but still refuses spaces and '#'.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML; there is no stylesheet or component UI, and no browser session was available.
No UI flow could be demonstrated; the diff has no front-end files beyond the HTML template.
The title is under 72 characters and the behaviour claims are accurate. The 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claim is not true of the named tests.
